A replica pirate ship called the Liana's Ransom ran into trouble about 30 miles off the coast of Maine on Monday. The ship reported that its engines had failed and that the sails were wrapped around the mast. Fearing for their safety, the crew was forced to abandon the ship. The U.S. Coast Guard rescued nine crew members from the ship using life boats. The ship was left drifting in the rough seas.

Amazing pictures have emerged of blue fluorescent algae lighting up Australia's east coast. The images were taken in Jervis Bay, the south coast of NSW, as the neon glow illuminated one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson described the sight as a 'beautiful supernatural scene' caused by millions of plankton omitting light. A similar display was shown in Sydney's Manly Beach back in August 2014 where an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia there was no need to be concerned about the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar climbed over a fence at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India, and ran toward the lions. He was drunk at the time. He shouted that he would kill the animals. Zoo security had to rescue him after he jumped into the enclosure.

A 12-year-old boy fell out of a five-story window and survived by landing on a car parked below. His father said the boy was probably sleepwalking when it happened. The accident happened last Saturday in Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi province in southeastern China, reported the People’s Daily Online. A worker at a hotel across the road said she heard a loud bang around midnight and thought it was a car accident.

Red Wings player Drew Miller is happy to be back on the ice just one day after getting a deep cut that could have hurt his eyesight. He feels very lucky the skate missed his eye. Miller was skating with a full face mask during practice on Wednesday. He had a nasty red wound across his face that needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. Another player cut him, leaving a scar across his eye. Luckily, he did not suffer any damage to his eyesight.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until the end of his contract. Even though Atletico Madrid wants to bring him back in the summer, he is happy at Chelsea and does not want to leave. He signed a three-year deal last year but has had trouble playing at the left back position. Atletico hope this may give them leverage, but Luis says he is happy and wants to stay until his contract ends.

A 20-year-old fan ran onto the pitch during a soccer game at the Madejski Stadium last month. Charlie Sumner did four front flips before stewards stopped him. He was trying to get onto the field for his first-ever game. Sumner was charged during Reading's 3-0 win over Bradford City. He now faces a three-year ban from soccer games.

A video shows a van carrying football fans swerving around a corner in Morocco. The vehicle toppled onto its side, sending the men riding on top into the air. The accident happened near the coastal city of Salé.

England have been drawn in Group D with the Republic of Ireland, Holland and Italy at the UEFA Under 17 European Championships in Bulgaria this May.

John Peacock's Young Lions are the defending champions after winning last year's final in Malta on penalties against Holland. To advance to the quarter-finals, they must overcome the Dutch again.

This is the first time the tournament has expanded from eight to 16 nations. Danny Collinge scored his first England goal in qualifying.

An angry elephant tried to spray a buffalo bull with water because it got too close. The elephant was relaxing in Kruger National Park in South Africa with its family by a small pool when the bull approached. In a video, the elephant squits water from its trunk to make the bull leave, but misses. The frustrated elephant tries again, but the bull keeps drinking. The young elephant hugs its parent for safety.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, has had his conviction overturned after an eight-year legal fight. He was originally convicted in 2006 for showing a Premier League game on foreign TV without a license. Although he has won his case, he lost his pub in Plymouth as a result of the legal battle.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage at its Windsor Park home in Belfast might prevent the team from playing a crucial Euro 2016 qualifier against Romania in June. Cracks were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning, and the area was closed off while engineers checked it. The Irish FA learned on Tuesday morning that overnight damage had happened to the West Stand of the National Football Stadium at Windsor Park. Northern Ireland's Windsor Park suffered overnight damage to its West Stand on Monday night.

A 20-year-old football fan has been banned for three years after running onto the pitch without a shirt and doing somersaults during his first time at the stadium.

Charlie Sumner went onto the pitch at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA cup quarter final replay with Bradford City last month. The fan, whose team were 3-0 up at the time, did four front flips on the pitch, landing on his back each time, before being tackled by stewards.

A man driving a BMW car with five children inside was arrested today. He hit and killed Hina Shamim, a 21-year-old student, as she walked to the library near Kingston University in London. Miss Shamim, who was from Peterborough and nicknamed "Hyena," was killed just weeks before her 22nd birthday. Friends left flowers at the scene, remembering her as "much-loved and the most charming lovely girl in the world."

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a student at a high school was posted online. The pair were caught on camera at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. The mother was reportedly angry with the girl because she had allegedly been bullying her daughter. The mother is seen in a black top on the right, and the victim is in the center wearing white.

Stoke chief executive Tony Scholes wants to keep goalkeeper Asmir Begovic at the club. Begovic has one year left on his contract and has been linked with other teams. Scholes says he can match Begovic's ambitions because he is a "terrific goalkeeper." Scholes notes that good players often attract interest from other clubs.

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand was filmed by a passenger while reading a newspaper. The driver was seen flicking through the pages while the bus was moving. The passenger sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, along with a complaint. The company's boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver's actions and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says Winston Reid will play on Saturday. Reid injured his hamstring in a game against Chelsea on March 4, but he is now fit after training during the break. Enner Valencia will not play because he hurt his toe at home in mid-Mrta and is not match fit.

Five days before their wedding last May, a car crash on a Georgia highway killed Brittany Huber and left her fiancé, John Redman, fighting for his life. Doctors told the 25-year-old that he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, confined to a wheelchair. However, against all the odds, Redman recovered. On March 24, he helped lead his team to a championship title.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during Sunday's All-Star charity game at Anfield. Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is trying to get back to his best form after recovering from injury. The Brazil international started 16 games out of 19 from late November. This helped the team win more games. In February, a injury problem in a Merseyside derby saw him miss 10 games. He was an unused substitute in the defeat by Manchester United immediately before the international break, their first in the league since mid-December, but played 90 minutes in Sunday's All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama takes funny pictures of fathers and daughters. In the photos, the daughters are smiling at the camera while their fathers jump into the air and make dramatic poses. Aoyama’s new book, called "Daughter and Salary Man," shows these pictures.

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old. He is suspected of robbing a bank in broad daylight and running off with £3,000 in cash.

The robbery happened at 12:30pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff. Detectives have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is between 5ft 9in and 6ft, and was wearing black clothing.

The suspect is a white male with greying black hair and glasses. He was captured on camera inside the bank. Police say no one was injured during the robbery and they are confident the public will be able to identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has allowed Morocco to compete in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. Morocco was originally banned from the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined $1 million by the Confederation of African Football. The CAF also demanded an additional $9 million in compensation because Morocco pulled out due to fears related to the Ebola epidemic. Morocco can now compete after the initial ban was imposed.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer has done such a good job on loan at Celtic that he is ready to fight for a spot at Manchester City next year. This would stop Celtic manager Ronny Deila from keeping the young Belgian for another year, but Boyd thinks this is still a good thing. To Boyd, Denayer’s success can show other young players that moving to Celtic is a great choice for their career. Young defender Jason Denayer has impressed on loan at Celtic this season. The 19-year-old recently won his first cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing critics who had questioned his abilities. The 23-year-old had used those doubts as motivation. Despite a mixed-up season, manager Roy Hodgson kept faith in him. Townsend repaid that trust with a stunning equaliser in England's 1-1 friendly draw against Italy in Turin. He celebrated the goal with his Tottenham teammates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20 percent of Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The purchase was finalized at a special meeting on Tuesday, where the legal team representing "Wanda Madrid Investment" signed the papers to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million). The deal was first announced in January, but two special meetings were needed to finalize it. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin hopes to grow Atletico's brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone speaks to the media.

Antonio Conte returned to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw against England. He said the experience brought up "very fond memories," even though reports said he received death threats before the game.

Conte became Italy's boss in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli after Italy lost its World Cup group-stage last summer. His first seven months in charge have been "topsy-turvy."

Italy needed a late goal from Eder to rescue a 2-2 draw against Bulgaria last Saturday. Reports say Conte received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury on the eve of the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibernian can catch up to Rangers in the final part of the Scottish Championship season. His team, Dumbarton, have played against both sides already this year and will face them again before the season ends. While Rangers are winning at the moment, Murray thinks they might struggle to keep up their speed, and Hibernian could take second place off them.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet returned to England after playing for Belgium in Euro 2016 qualifiers against Cyprus and Israel. Although he was in the match-day squad for both games, he did not play. Chelsea's Thibaut Courtois was chosen as the starter instead, leaving Mignolet with 14 caps to his name. Mignolet posted photos of him posing in an aeroplane cockpit on his Facebook page on Wednesday.

A large rural estate is for sale at £6 million. It is near Bridgnorth, Shropshire, and covers 200 acres of land. The property has a Grade II-listed manor house and five cotties. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms and was built in 1814. There is also a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and its own cricket green. The secluded grounds offer complete privacy. It has only had two previous owners.

Two college campus police officers in Dallas have been placed on leave after a video showed them harassing a group of students and hitting one of them. The incident happened at El Centro College last Wednesday. Student Charles Adams recorded the video on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw the officers approach four students waiting for a bus outside the downtown campus. One student was hit and arrested.

Gary Locke has been made the permanent manager of Kilmarnock. He signed a three-year contract after doing the job temporarily since February. The 39-year-old, who previously worked with Allan Johnston, has lost only one game in seven since taking over. He will speak to the media on Friday.

This weekend, one of the biggest games on the German football schedule takes place. "Der Klassiker" is the name of the match between Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich. These two teams have won the last five German league titles between them, and Bayern are expected to win again this season.

Usually, this game is a close competition. However, the teams are not close in the current standings. Bayern is in first place, while Dortmund is ninth, with a gap of 31 points. Even though the standings are far apart, the importance of the match remains high.

Jurgen Klop (centre) celebrates with his Borussia Dortmund players after their victory against Hannover.

A 14-year-old girl was left stranded at a busy airport after easyJet refused to let her board her plane because she had two pieces of hand luggage. Deva Joseph was reduced to tears at London Stansted airport after being told she could not take her flight home to Spain. The teenager offered to pay for the second item to be put in the hold, but was told only credit cards would be accepted—even though she is too young to have one.

Gordon Robson, 26, punched John Potts, 45, in the back of the head outside a sports bar. The hit was so hard it made a loud cracking sound, and Mr. Potts fell down and died. Robson, who had a criminal record, was sentenced to three and a half years in jail.

Ellen White scored a free kick against her old team, Notts County. In the 26th minute, she spun around the edge of the box and hit the ball into the corner. This happened right after her teammates Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood almost crashed into each other while trying to set up the kick.

These are the amazing scenes as high school girls in China are put through their paces with military-style dagger drills. Each of the girls shout the words 'kill, stab, slash and jab' as they perform each of the eight set movements involved in the high-intensity knife-fighting session. According to the People's Daily Online, the girls of the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School are being trained by former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The 68 girls involved in the training are all aged between 16 and 18, however in a concession to safety, the knives are not real. School official Huang Anruo said: 'The daggers are fake.'

We spend about a third of our lives sleeping. However, most people do not think about what their mind and body need during these resting hours to feel refreshed.

According to the Sleep Health Foundation, 30 percent of Australians complain about a lack of sleep every day. Professor David Hillman says that lost sleep must be "paid back" to function properly during the week. The average adult needs about eight hours of sleep per night, with a recommended range of seven to nine hours.

A video posted on Facebook shows a heated argument between neighbours in a Perth suburb. The argument escalated into a physical confrontation where a woman brandished a crowbar and shouted racist insults at a group of men. The men responded by picking up their own weapons, and a scuffle ensued.

Everyone is watching Valencia's 19-year-old left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea want to sign him this summer, but Real Madrid also wants him. Sportswriter Pete Jenson looks at the Spain under 21 defender.

Why are English clubs so keen? His buy-out clause is currently set at £13.5m. When you consider that Luke Shaw – of a similar age and potential – cost £27m, it would be silly not to be interested. However, there would also be reservations about his suitability to the Premier League. Jose Luis Gaya (right) in action for Valencia during a La Liga match with Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help finding a man on a green motorcycle. He is a hero who stopped a bad guy named Edward West, 59, from threatening two teens with a gun. The stranger jumped onto the scene, used his helmet to knock the gun away, and let the teens run away.

Tim Sherwood has asked Ron Vlaar to prove himself again as Aston Villa's captain gets ready to play. Sherwood wants to see the fit defender help the struggling team finish well. He warned that people might have forgotten Vlaar's heroics at the World Cup last year. Vlaar starred in Holland's run to the semi finals in Brazil, despite missing a penalty in the shoot-out against Argentina. This led to links with Manchester United. Aston Villa will welcome back club captain Ron Vlaar as they head to Old Trafford on Saturday. The commanding Dutch centre-back returns from injury to help Villa in their battle against relegation.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover of Aston Villa this summer. He plans to build a team in his style for next season, but this depends on the team staying up in the league. Randy Lerner is in talks with a possible new owner. If a new owner comes in, people will question Sherwood's job. But Sherwood is focused on keeping the team up first, and then he will make big changes in the summer.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a takeover. Christian Benteke scored a goal as Aston Villa beat Sunderland last month.

Celtic hoped to keep Jason Denyer on loan from Manchester City for next season. However, Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola said his young Academy players are not ready for the first team. So, Denyer might have to return to City to play there instead. Denyer has done well while on loan at Celtic this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a more specific date for Fraser Forster's return before deciding if he needs to sign a new goalkeeper this summer. Forster had knee surgery after getting hurt in Southampton's 2-0 win over Burnley a couple of weeks ago. Experts say he might be back in four to 12 months. Koeman does not want to give a exact time for the England player yet. He thinks Kelvin Davis can fill in, but he might have to get another keeper if Forster is slow to get better.

Rotherham boss Steve Evans was angry on the sidelines after his team, which is in danger of being relegated, was denied a penalty in their narrow Championship defeat at Birmingham. The hosts had led through first-half goals by Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson, before Matt Derbyshire pulled one back for fourth-bottom Rotherham. However, Rob Kiernan's clumsy handling of Derbyshire near the hour mark saw the former City forward go down in the box only for referee Dean Whitestone to wave away appeals for a spot-kick, leaving the Millers boss visibly enraged as the home side held out. Robert Tesche of Birmingham City celebrates scoring the opening goal of the game.

The worry about Virgil van Dijk is clear. Holland’s national team has already let more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifiers than they did in the entire qualifying campaign for the last World Cup. And still, Guus Hiddink never calls or writes. The Celtic defender made it into two squads last year. But one step forward is usually followed by two steps back. When the Dutch were drawing 1-1 with Turkey the other night he was sunning himself in the Arabian Gulf and bumping into club-mates instead. Virgil van Dijk has been in fine form for Celtic but wasn't rewarded with a call-up to the Holland national team.

Celtic have complained to the Scottish Football Association (SFA) about the ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness this month at Hampden Park.

The governing body that runs Scottish football has already come under criticism from Inverness fans for scheduling the game for 12:15pm on Sunday, April 18 - before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow.

Now the Parkhead club have made their feelings known after ticket prices were set at £23 for the North and South stands, with the East Stand being £15 for adults and £5 for concessions.

Rangers interim chairman Paul Murray said on Thursday night that previous boardroom regimes were "solely" to blame for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The Ibrox outfit will be forced to delist from the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) after being unable to secure a new nominated advisor (Nomad) to meet regulations. Murray insists the new board’s plans for the future will be unaffected and that planned investments will still take place.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were upset by their poor start against Italy on Tuesday night. It was their first meeting since the World Cup nine months ago. High hopes were raised by seven straight wins, but Roy Hodgson's team struggled in the first half. They fell behind to a header by Graziano Pelle. Wayne Rooney gave instructions during the 1-1 draw. He said he and the rest of the England players were upset by their first half performance.

Dundee United's two main fan groups are angry about how the club's leaders are doing their jobs. They are upset that 25 percent of the money made from selling four players was paid as a fee to unknown people. The groups also disagree with the chairman's claim that he has put a lot of money into the club. The board says the fans' criticism is wrong because the team is doing well on the field.

Gary Locke will be announced as Kilmarnock's permanent manager on Friday. The 39-year-old, who took over as a temporary boss in February, has been given a three-year contract. He replaces Allan Johnston and will lead the club under new chairman Jim Mann.

Chinese parents love raising children who are very talented. Some are even getting into university at age 10, while others are four-year-olds dancing like Michael Jackson.

A new basketball star is becoming popular in China. A video is going viral there, showing a small boy with amazing basketball skills that shock even professional players. The boy is five years old and named Mai Zizhuo. He started shooting hoops when he was two and a half, reported People's Daily Online. The video starts with the small player scoring many hoops while dribbling two basketballs at the same time.

Bayern Munich will miss David Alaba for the rest of the season. The 22-year-old injured his knee while playing for Austria against Bosnia on Tuesday. Doctors say he is out for about seven weeks. Alaba had been out for three months earlier this season with a knee injury. He said he was "disappointed" but wants to play in the final game of the season.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse from Canberra Raiders to fill the gap left by Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey. The 6ft 7in, 17st-plus Tilse has agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal and will join the Robins as soon as paperwork is complete. At 30 years old with 200 appearances for Canberra, Tilse will link up with teammate Terry Campese and acts as a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month due to injury.

Livingston boss Mark Burchill thinks Darren Cole wants to play in Sunday's final, just a week after his cousin died in America. The ex-Rangers player has been mourning Shaun Cole, 22, who was found dead in a Miami street last weekend. He was a soldier who served in Afghanistan and was on holiday in Florida. Burchill is hopeful Darren Cole will play for his side on Sunday.

Alan Smith has denied claims that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was traveling to the hospital in after his serious injury during Manchester United's 1-0 defeat to their rivals nine years ago.

Smith suffered a broken leg and a dislocated ankle while trying to block a John Arne Riise free-kick during the fifth round clash at Anfield in February 2006.

At the time, reports circulated that Liverpool fans tried to disrupt Smith's journey to hospital by throwing bottles, beer glasses and stones at the ambulance as well as rocking the vehicle.

C manager Ronny Deila says Celtic want to buy Hearts captain Danny Wilson. The Scottish champions are thinking about making a £400,000 offer for the defender. Wilson has one year left on his contract with Hearts. The club owner, Ann Budge, says they do not need to sell him. Wilson is a free agent at the end of the season.

Ronny Deila says Celtic will not travel to other countries before the Champions League starts. He blamed last summer's games in the US, Austria, and Germany for the team's 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw. Celtic makes money by playing pre-season games in places like Australia and Asia. Ronny Deila and Nir Bitton left the field after that loss. A trip to America this July is still possible.

Franck Ribery has denied reports that Kevin de Bruyne could replace him or his teammate Arjen Robben at Bayern Munich. De Bruyne, who joined the second-placed Bundesliga club after spending two years on loan at Chelsea, has scored nine goals and leads the league in assists with 16. However, Ribery says despite the impressive form, the 23-year-old Belgian is the wrong style of player to fit into Pep Guardiola's system because he has different assets than Ribery and the Holland winger.
